 9        from the University of St. Thomas, St. Paul, and a Bachelor of Science in Chemical

16        working as a Loss Control Consultant for Xcel Energy where I advised on property

17        and mechanical exposures. Before joining Xcel Energy, I worked at Cargill Inc. as

18        an Environment, Health, and Safety Engineer providing technical support for

 1                 II.    PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY
 2   Q.   What is the overall purpose of your direct testimony in this proceeding?

 3   A.   The purpose of my testimony is to support the reasonableness of: (1) the Excess

 4        Liability Insurance (“ELI”) costs SPS has deferred into a regulatory asset in

 5        accordance with the Commission’s final order in Docket No. 25-00030-UT;

 6        (2) SPS’s strategy for the procurement of ELI; and (3) SPS’s efforts to mitigate the

 7        cost of ELI going forward in the face of significant short-term price volatility in the

 8        ELI market. To that end, my direct testimony provides an overview of SPS’s

 9        insurance program, historical information on insurance premiums, addresses

10        changing conditions, provides information on SPS’s recent renewal of insurance

11        policies for ELI, and addresses my perspective on the likelihood of future volatility

12        in insurance markets and options SPS may have to insure.

13   Q.   Please summarize your testimony.

14   A.   Xcel Energy began to see increased pressure on ELI premiums in 2023, and by

15        January 2024, the expectation that the next renewal would face potentially material

16        increases in premiums was known. By the time SPS’s policy renewal was executed

17        in October 2024, SPS incurred an approximate $31 million increase in premiums

18        despite a reduction in coverage. In response to this extreme volatility that has no

19        historical basis, SPS filed an application in Docket No. 25-00030-UT requesting

                                                4
                                           Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                             Direct Testimony
                                                     of
                                             Robert L. Miller

 1           Commission authorization to defer ELI premium amounts above SPS’s 2023 per

 2           book expense for evaluation in SPS’s next base rate case.

 3                    After a hearing on the merits, the Hearing Examiner filed a Recommended

4            Decision, which found that SPS’s request should be approved and SPS should be

5            allowed a one-time accounting order to track and preserve costs associated with the

 6           increase in its ELI premiums. 2 Specifically, the Hearing Examiner found that the

 7           requirements for an “extraordinary” event are satisfied, which further supports

 8           granting SPS’s requested accounting order. 3 The Commission agreed that issuing

 9           an accounting order is in the public interest because a utility having insurance is

10           reasonable and expected, even with a significant increase in the cost of ELI, in order

11           to insure the electric system and operator of the system that serves the customer. 4

12           The Commission further concluded that exceptional circumstances surrounding the

13           increase in ELI premiums justified issuance of the accounting order because the

14           increase in SPS’s ELI premium was material; unplanned; beyond SPS’s control;

15           and unusual, abnormal, and unlikely to be repeated. 5 Finally, the Commission

 1        III.   EXCESS LIABILITY INSURANCE PREMIUM BACKGROUND

 2   Q.    What is the purpose of this section of your direct testimony?

 3   A.    I explain what excess liability insurance is and what it covers. I also describe how

 4         SPS has historically recovered ELI premiums and the specific factors that drove

 5         SPS’s need for an accounting order and authorization to defer these increased

 6         premiums into a regulatory asset.

 7   Q.    Why does SPS obtain insurance?

 8   A.    Like any business, SPS purchases insurance to prudently protect against a variety

 9         of business risks. SPS takes steps on a continuing basis to make certain that the

10         insurance program provides proper risk protection necessary to deliver safe,

11         reliable, and cost-effective utility service to customers. By insuring against

12         potential liabilities rather than taking on the risk of liabilities, the associated costs

13         have historically been steadier and more predictable. In the long term, this results

14         in lower and more consistent rates for customers.




                                                  7
                                     Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                       Robert L. Miller

 1   Q.   Does Xcel Energy obtain insurance across its business enterprises or do

 2        individual operating companies within Xcel Energy, like SPS, acquire their

 3        own insurance?

 4   A.   In most cases, Xcel Energy is the holder of insurance policies. The operating

 5        companies, including SPS, are all named insureds, so that there is coverage for each

 6        entity as needed as claims arise. The costs are then allocated or directly assigned,

 7        as applicable, to the individual operating companies, as I explain further below.

 8        While not applicable to SPS, an exception to this is for nuclear property and liability

 9        insurance. These assets are within one single operating company and associated

10        insurance is not purchased on a holding company basis. Another exception is when

11        builders’ risk insurance is specifically purchased for an individual project within

12        one of the operating companies. Neither of these costs are further allocated.

13   Q.   What types of coverages does Xcel Energy’s insurance generally have for the

14        benefit of SPS?

15   A.   Xcel Energy maintains several different types of insurance. Broadly, the

16        composition of Xcel Energy’s insurance program is based on several

17        considerations:

18           •   Statutory requirements such as workers’ compensation requirements or
19               professional liability requirements;

                                                8
                                    Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                      Robert L. Miller

 1           •   Obligations to protect assets that are financed by third parties under
 2               mortgage indentures and other covenants;

 3           •   Benchmarking against utility industry peers;

 4           •   Analytics performed internally as well as by third parties that evaluate the
 5               frequency and severity of loss to optimize financing costs; and

 6           •   Balancing long-term costs of the insurance program against the risks of
 7               being insured, to ensure insurance costs and insured risks are reasonably
 8               level over the long term.

 9               Notably, Xcel Energy procures ELI for the benefit of SPS, along with its

10        other Operating Companies. ELI is intended to insure SPS against liability to third

11        parties. Examples of claims paid under this policy include property damage or

12        bodily injury to third parties caused by Xcel Energy Services, Inc. or SPS

13        employees, equipment, or facilities.

14   Q.   How does ELI obtained by Xcel Energy benefit SPS?

15   A.   It is important for SPS to have financial protection from catastrophic claims it may

16        face while providing service for its customers. Absent ELI, there could be claims

17        against SPS that would significantly and negatively impact its cash flow and credit

18        metrics, which in turn would raise SPS’s financing costs and overall cost of

19        providing utility service to customers. All else equal, that would cause an increase

20        in customer rates.



                                                 9
                                     Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                       Robert L. Miller

 1   Q.   Please discuss how ELI is structured.

 2   A.   The ELI program is primarily a layered structure. The layered structure is an

 3        industry convention for the placement of insurance, whereby different underwriters

 4        undertake a certain portion of total insured risk for any particular program. For

 5        example, in a hypothetical structure of three layers (or policies), with each layer

 6        providing $5 million of coverage, SPS would be insured for claims up to a total of

 7        $15 million. If a $7 million loss were then incurred, the insurer providing the first,

 8        or bottom, layer would pay its full $5 million limit, and the next insurer would pay

 9        $2 million. This structure has many advantages: (1) it provides credit exposure

10        protections to SPS; (2) it provides additional risk protection to insurance

11        underwriters, which decreases the level of risk they are insuring thereby driving

12        down premiums; and (3) it mitigates each insurance underwriter’s overall financial

13        exposure to SPS, meaning each insurance company’s limit is exhausted before the

14        next insurance company begins to respond to a claim. The insurance industry refers

15        to this layered structure as a “tower.”

16               The entire tower of insurers makes up the total limit of insurance purchased.

17        The first layers of the tower are comprised of mutual insurance companies. Mutual

18        insurers’ policies generally provide broader coverage and more stable pricing than


                                                10
                                    Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                      Robert L. Miller

 1        commercial markets. In addition, in times of lower losses from claims, they return

 2        a portion of premiums paid back to the members, which in turn are credited against

 3        renewal premiums. Examples of these pools are Associated Electric & Gas

 4        Insurances Services (“AEGIS”), Energy Insurance Mutual (“EIM”), and Cedar

 5        Hamilton. The higher layers of the tower involve insurance obtained through the

 6        commercial insurance markets, which can have greater cost fluctuations for

 7        insurance coverage than that provided by mutual insurers. An additional element of

 8        the tower involves our long-standing segregated cell insurance captive that provides

 9        insurance to Xcel Energy and its subsidiaries, like SPS. The insurance captive fills

10        in gaps throughout the tower to optimize it.

11   Q.   How does Xcel Energy allocate ELI premiums to SPS?

12   A.   ELI costs are generally allocated in three ways. First, when sufficient information

13        is available from insurers to determine the portion of premiums attributable to

14        specific operating companies, such as SPS, based on risk quantifications of those

15        individual operating companies, such amounts are direct assigned to the responsible

16        operating company. Second, a portion of premiums may be direct assigned based

17        on historical claims, such that operating companies receive premium allocations

18        consistent with historical claim results. The remaining and general balance of the


                                              11
                                          Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                            Direct Testimony
                                                    of
                                            Robert L. Miller

 1           premiums is then allocated in accordance with established affiliate cost allocation

 2           methodologies. These internal allocation methods are supported by SPS witness

 3           Nichole L. Doyle.

 4   Q.      Historically, how much of Xcel Energy’s ELI premiums have been allocated to

 5           SPS?

 6   A.      The ELI premium was fairly stable year-over-year for both Xcel Energy and SPS

 7           between 2014 and 2020, with slight increases during that time. Then, as shown in

 8           Table RLM-1 below, for the 2021 insurance renewal that took place in August 2021,

 9           the insurance markets saw increased claims activity and higher risks and began

10           applying a higher premium. As discussed in SPS’s last base rate case, overall

11           insurance cost increases from 2019 to 2020 were primarily driven by increases in

12           ELI premiums. From 2021 through 2022 (the end of the Base Period and start of

13           the Linkage Period in SPS’s most recent base rate case, Case No. 22-00286-UT),

14           overall insurance costs were relatively consistent. 7

2    Q.       How does Xcel Energy seek to limit the costs associated with insurance

3             premiums?

4    A.       Xcel Energy has a variety of processes in place to ensure not only the appropriate

5             levels and types of insurance but also to ensure that costs are reasonable. Below are

6             some of the procurement and review efforts we engage in:

 7               •     Use of specialized and expert insurance brokers to assist with matching
 8                     qualified insurers with business needs and to help inform whether the
 9                     pricing obtained is reasonable. This process typically starts six months
10                     before the renewal date of insurance policies. Brokers have extensive
11                     experience working with similar companies and have deep industry
12                     knowledge about available products and reasonable premiums.

13               •     Active participation in various insurance markets around the world,
14                     including the US commercial market, European markets (including Lloyd’s


                                                        13
                                    Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                      Robert L. Miller

 1              of London), Bermuda markets, and through industry mutual insurance
 2              companies.

3          •    To ensure Xcel Energy is receiving appropriate coverage and paying
4               appropriate premiums, meetings are held with each underwriter in each
5               insurance market to explain the risk profiles, the types of claims that have
6               been historically made, and to discuss forecasted risks.

 7         •    Xcel Energy ensures that potential underwriters are creditworthy and works
 8              directly with them to develop the policy terms. The general insurance policy
 9              and premium negotiations are extensive and involve many individual
10              meetings with underwriters. Senior management, as well as relevant
11              business unit representatives, are actively involved in these negotiations to
12              ensure that underwriters have a thorough understanding of risks, risk
13              management practices, and operational excellence. Through these meetings
14              and negotiations, Xcel Energy is able to differentiate its operations from
15              utility peers. This, combined with unique risk mitigation efforts including
16              establishment of plans that mitigate and/or reduce risk for utility
17              infrastructure or operations, ultimately results in what Xcel Energy
18              understands and have heard to be better terms and conditions and
19              competitive premiums as compared to peers. 8 An approved WMP will likely
20              carry increased significance in the future as utilities evaluate wildfire risk
21              transfer options.

22         •    Xcel Energy has developed long-term relationships with key insurers to
23              develop confidence and trust. To that end, we meet several times each year
24              with underwriters to discuss current issues in an effort to allow underwriters
25              to understand risk profiles better and feel more comfortable insuring SPS’s
26              risk.

27         •    In addition, we also have several programs and review processes in place
28              internally to manage costs and reduce claims. These include monitoring
29              industry losses and ensuring measures are in place to prevent similar events
30              at Xcel Energy; implementing a particular focus on safety performance and

1                training programs; and executing corporate procedures and policies that
2                help reduce the potential for claims.

3    Q.   What is the premium from the current excess liability policy that is allocated

4         to SPS?

5    A.   For October 2024 through October 2025, the premiums for SPS were

 6        approximately $42.6 million (total company). This total amount included

 7        approximately $5.3 million (total company) of allocated premiums, with the

 8        remainder directly assigned to SPS. This policy expired October 18, 2025. I will

9         discuss the renewed ELI policy in the next section of my testimony.

10   Q.   Did other utilities experience similar increases in premiums during the 2023

11        to 2024 time period?

12   A.   Yes. Renewal premiums of some industry peers increased by as much as 700

13        percent.

14   Q.   What drove the increase in ELI premiums?

15   A.   The increased wildfire risk and associated wildfire claims are primary drivers of

16        the increase in premiums in the excess liability markets, especially in the west.

17        Numerous wildfire claims against utilities are causing the insurance market to

18        reduce their insurance capacity and increase the price of insurance they will

19        continue to provide.

 1          IV.     RENEWED EXCESS LIABILITY INSURANCE POLICY

 2   Q.   What is the purpose of this section of your direct testimony?

 3   A.   In this section of my direct testimony, I discuss Xcel Energy’s recent renewal of its

 4        ELI policy, summarize the significantly increased premiums, the basis for that

 5        increase, and how the future of these premiums is expected to be volatile despite

 6        Xcel Energy’s and SPS’s actions and explorations of ways to stabilize the

 7        premiums.

 8   Q.   How has Xcel Energy approached the process to renew its ELI policy?

 9   A.   Protecting the wide array of Xcel Energy operations and assets requires input and

10        coordination with many business units and departments, as well as outside experts.

11        SPS has generally had a similar insurance structure in place for the past 20 years.

12        However, the insurance policies are on one-year terms, and thus need to be

13        renegotiated on an annual basis. Prior to each renewal, Xcel Energy performs a

14        fresh evaluation of risks and alternatives to ensure that the insurance program

15        continues to appropriately balance costs and benefits. The state of the insurance

16        market is also evaluated for each different type of risk insured to inform what may

17        be encountered as part of the renewal. Insurance needs are determined by:




                                               16
                                     Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                       Direct Testimony
                                               of
                                       Robert L. Miller

1            •   Reviewing current insurance programs through analytics to determine if
2                they still match the current risk profile and are cost effective, or if any
3                additional coverage or levels might be appropriate to obtain given current
4                market conditions;

5            •   Conferring with experts to identify trends or potential issues and benchmark
6                our costs to industry norms; and

7            •   Working with experienced insurance brokers who handle similar clients and
8                bring additional risk management experience to the decision.

 9   Q.   When did negotiations begin to renew the current ELI policy?

10   A.   As Xcel Energy knew this would be a challenging renewal given evolving wildfire

11        risk across the western United States and rising premium expectations, Xcel Energy

12        began the process in January 2025.

13   Q.   When did negotiations conclude and when did the new ELI policy take effect?

14   A.   The entire program tower was negotiated and in place in early October 2025. The

15        new policy took effect on October 18, 2025.

16   Q.   What steps has Xcel Energy taken to attempt to lower the anticipated

17        insurance premium increase?

18   A.   I previously addressed our actions to seek to limit insurance costs. In addition to

19        those actions, we are specifically educating our insurers on our wildfire mitigation

20        activities. This educational effort assists in differentiating our risk from our peers

21        and at times will provide us access to additional capacity and preferred pricing.

                                               17
                                           Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                             Direct Testimony
                                                     of
                                             Robert L. Miller

 1        Further, we have approached new insurance markets to replace the capacity that is

 2        being cut by some insurers due to wildfire risks, to ensure we have the appropriate

 3        level of coverage.

 4                   As a result of these efforts, the ELI program structure was modified in 2025

 5        at an increased premium of approximately 6% on an Xcel Energy enterprise basis

 6        for similar insurance limits. If the structure had remained the same, it is estimated

 7        to have resulted in an increase of premium in excess of 15% for similar insurance

 8        limits.

 9   Q.   Did the renewed policy result in increased insurance premiums for SPS?

10   A.   Yes. The total premium increase for SPS is from approximately $42.6 million (total

11        company) to an estimated $45.8 million 9 (total company) (new policy cost), which

12        represents almost a 7.5 percent increase.

13   Q.   How do those costs compare to historical insurance premiums for SPS?

14   A.   As shown in Table RLM-1, the new premium for the renewed ELI policies slightly

15        exceeds the premium SPS experienced in 2024, but still greatly exceeds the

16        premiums SPS experienced back to 2014. There is really no analogous historical

17        premium cost increase to that occurring for the past two renewals.

1    Q.   Do you find an increase in insurance premium to be remarkable, and if so,

2         why?

3    A.   While SPS’s 2025 ELI premium increase is 7.5%, this is on top of the over 300%

4         increase in 2024 when compared to 2023. As noted above, this two-year level of

5         ELI costs for SPS is unprecedented. Similar increases have been previously seen in

6         other western states, such as California, but now Colorado, New Mexico, and Texas

7         are being placed in a similar category for excess liability insurance underwriting

8         purposes. Other utilities, such as PacifiCorp, have seen their insurance premiums

9         increase more than 400 percent. Unfortunately, premium increases of a similar

10        nature are now impacting SPS.

11   Q.   Does the renewed policy inform your perspective of what the future may hold

12        for insurance premiums for SPS?

13   A.   The risk associated with wildfire injects much uncertainty in the third-party liability

14        insurance market. It is an industry-wide challenge that will continue to impact our

15        insurance programs along with the rest of the utility sector, with the potential for

16        variability in not only pricing, but also the terms of the coverage as well. While

17        mitigating our own wildfire risk helps provide more stability in the insurance




                                                19
                                    Case No. 25-00____-UT
                                      Direct Testimony
                                              of
                                      Robert L. Miller

 1        market, we are also dependent on the industry as a whole to improve the overall

 2        risk profile.

 3   Q.   Could insurance premiums decrease in the future?

 4   A.   Yes, they could. The insurance rating process is made up of two parts. The

 5        underwriters will look at the exposure and develop a price based on the insured’s

 6        risk and the history of loss. The insurer may then price the policy based on the

 7        higher of the two or a blend. In the future, Xcel Energy expects to see insurance

 8        premiums decrease as wildfire mitigation activities continue to reduce risks, as

 9        other utilities’ wildfire mitigation plans become more developed, and as overall

10        industry losses decrease. Additionally, as explained further by SPS witness Zoë E.

11        Lees, there could be federal or state legislative changes to also decrease insurance

12        premiums. These results will likely encourage new insurance marketers to offer

13        policies and improve the ability of existing marketers to potentially increase their

14        offered capacity. The competition may reasonably drive the price down over time.

15   Q.   Generally, do you expect the premium for excess liability insurance to remain

16        consistent going forward?

17   A.   No. Due to the changing and emerging wildfire risk across the United States, I

18        expect that premiums for excess liability insurance for Xcel Energy and SPS will
